stem: Best guess: an individual has a $10,000 net capital loss and no other capital transactions. How much can be deducted against ordinary income this year?

choices.explanation: Correct. Individuals deduct up to $3,000 of net capital loss per year; the rest carries forward.

explanation: Individuals deduct up to $3,000 of net capital loss per year; the rest carries forward.

stem: A C corporation has a $20,000 net capital loss and $500,000 of ordinary income. How much capital loss may it deduct this year?

choices.explanation: Corporations can't deduct capital losses against ordinary income.
Correct. Corporate capital losses offset only capital gains; excess is carried back 3 and forward 5 years as short-term losses.

explanation: Corporate capital losses offset only capital gains; excess is carried back 3 and forward 5 years as short-term losses.

stem: Equipment used in a business (cost $50,000; accumulated depreciation $30,000) is sold for $35,000. What is the character of the gain?

choices.explanation: Correct. Gain of $15,000 is less than the $30,000 of depreciation.
Recapture is limited to the gain.

explanation: Gain = 35,000 − 20,000 = 15,000, all recaptured as ordinary because depreciation (30,000) exceeds it.

stem: Which asset is a capital asset in the hands of the taxpayer?

choices.text: Inventory held for sale by a retailer
Equipment used in the taxpayer's business
Stock held as an investment by an individual
choices.explanation: Correct. §1221 excludes inventory, receivables, depreciable business property, and business real property.

choices.text: Accounts receivable from sales of inventory
choices.explanation: Receivables from business sales are excluded.

explanation: §1221 excludes inventory, receivables, depreciable business property, and business real property.

stem: An individual has a short-term gain of $6,000 and a long-term loss of $10,000. What is the result?

choices.text: $4,000 net long-term capital loss, fully deductible this year
choices.explanation: Only $3,000 of the $4,000 net loss is deductible this year.

choices.text: $6,000 short-term gain taxed; $10,000 loss carried forward

explanation: Net: 6,000 − 10,000 = (4,000) long-term. Deduct 3,000; carry forward 1,000 long-term.

stem: What is the maximum rate on long-term gain from selling collectibles such as art or coins?

choices.explanation: Correct. Collectibles gain is taxed at a maximum of 28%.

explanation: Collectibles gain is taxed at a maximum of 28%.

stem: An individual sells a rental building for a $200,000 gain; straight-line depreciation taken was $80,000. How much is unrecaptured §1250 gain?

choices.explanation: Correct. Unrecaptured §1250 gain = lesser of the gain or straight-line depreciation = 80,000, taxed at a maximum of 25%.
Only gain up to depreciation taken.

explanation: Unrecaptured §1250 gain = lesser of the gain or straight-line depreciation = 80,000, taxed at a maximum of 25%.

stem: A C corporation sells a building for a $300,000 gain; straight-line depreciation was $100,000. How much is ordinary income under §291?

choices.explanation: 20% of the gain, not of the lesser amount.

stem: This year, a taxpayer has a net §1231 gain of $50,000. Two years ago she had a net §1231 loss of $15,000 (none recaptured yet). How is this year's gain characterized?

choices.explanation: The lookback recaptures prior losses as ordinary.
Only the lookback amount is ordinary.
Correct. 5-year lookback: net §1231 gain is ordinary to the extent of nonrecaptured §1231 losses of the prior 5 years.

explanation: 5-year lookback: net §1231 gain is ordinary to the extent of nonrecaptured §1231 losses of the prior 5 years.

stem: A net §1231 loss for the year is treated as:

choices.text: A capital loss subject to the $3,000 limit

choices.explanation: Correct. Net §1231 losses are ordinary — fully deductible.

choices.text: A long-term capital loss carried forward
choices.explanation: Net §1231 losses are ordinary, not capital.

explanation: Net §1231 losses are ordinary — fully deductible.

stem: A married couple filing jointly sells §1244 stock at a $130,000 loss. How much is an ordinary loss?

choices.explanation: Correct. §1244 allows ordinary loss up to $50,000 ($100,000 MFJ); the excess is capital loss.
That's the cap for single filers.
That's the net capital loss limit.

explanation: §1244 allows ordinary loss up to $50,000 ($100,000 MFJ); the excess is capital loss.

stem: Stock purchased on March 10, Year 1 is sold on March 10, Year 2. What is the holding period?

choices.text: Long-term, because it was held one year
choices.explanation: Must be held more than one year.

choices.text: It depends on the amount of the gain
Short-term; it must be held over one year
choices.explanation: Correct. Long-term requires holding more than one year; the day of acquisition is excluded, and the sale day is included — March 10 to March 10 is exactly one year.

choices.text: Long-term only if it is sold at a gain
choices.explanation: Gain or loss doesn't change the holding period.

explanation: Long-term requires holding more than one year; the day of acquisition is excluded, and the sale day is included — March 10 to March 10 is exactly one year.

stem: Equipment (cost $80,000; accumulated depreciation $50,000) is sold for $95,000. What is the character of the $65,000 gain?
explanation: Gain = 95,000 − 30,000 = 65,000. §1245 ordinary = 50,000 (depreciation); remaining 15,000 (above original cost) is §1231.

stem: An individual has STCG $8,000, STCL $3,000, LTCG $2,000 and LTCL $9,000. What is the effect on taxable income?

choices.explanation: Correct. Net ST gain $5,000 less net LT loss $7,000.

explanation: Net ST: +$5,000; net LT: −$7,000. Netting gives a $2,000 net capital loss, deductible against ordinary income.

stem: A single taxpayer has a $10,000 net short-term capital loss and no other capital transactions. What is the treatment?
explanation: Individuals deduct up to $3,000 of net capital loss per year; the excess carries forward indefinitely, keeping its character.

stem: What is the annual net capital loss deduction limit for a married taxpayer filing separately?

choices.explanation: That is the limit for other filers.

explanation: §1211(b): the limit is $3,000, or $1,500 for married filing separately.

stem: How long may an individual carry forward an unused net capital loss?

choices.explanation: Correct. Individuals carry losses forward until used.

explanation: Individuals carry net capital losses forward indefinitely; corporations carry them back 3 and forward 5 years.

stem: An individual sells her personal car, bought for $30,000, for $18,000. How is the $12,000 loss treated?

choices.explanation: Correct. Losses on personal-use assets are nondeductible.

explanation: A personal-use asset is a capital asset, but a loss on its sale isn't deductible.

stem: A donee sells stock at a gain 4 months after receiving it. The donor held it for 3 years. What is the holding period?

choices.explanation: Gifts tack when basis carries over.
Correct. Carryover basis brings a tacked period.

explanation: §1223(2): when the donee's basis is the donor's basis, the donor's holding period is added.

stem: Stock bought on November 1, Year 1 becomes worthless in March, Year 2. How is the loss treated?

choices.explanation: The deemed sale date makes it long-term.
Correct. It's treated as sold on December 31, Year 2.

explanation: §165(g): a security that becomes worthless is treated as sold on the last day of the tax year, so the holding period runs to December 31.

stem: For 2025, the 0% capital gains rate applies to single filers with taxable income up to $48,350. A single filer has $40,000 of taxable income, including $5,000 of LTCG. At what rate is the LTCG taxed?

choices.explanation: Correct. Taxable income is below the 0% breakpoint.

explanation: Long-term capital gain falling within the 0% bracket (up to $48,350 for single filers in 2025) is taxed at 0%.

stem: An artist sells a painting she created herself. How is the gain characterized?

choices.explanation: Correct. Self-created artworks aren't capital assets.
It isn't a capital asset to her.

explanation: §1221(a)(3): artistic works held by the taxpayer whose personal efforts created them aren't capital assets.

stem: An individual has a $10,000 net long-term gain from collectibles and a $4,000 net short-term loss. How much gain is taxed at the 28% rate?

choices.explanation: Correct. A net ST loss offsets the 28% group first.

explanation: A net short-term capital loss offsets 28% gain first, then 25% gain, then 15%/20% gain.

stem: An individual carries a $5,000 long-term capital loss into the year and has an $8,000 short-term gain. How is the year's result taxed?

choices.explanation: The carryforward nets with the gain.
The loss offsets this year's gain.
Correct. The LT loss offsets the ST gain.

explanation: Carryforward losses keep their character and net with the year's gains: −$5,000 LT and +$8,000 ST give a $3,000 net short-term gain.
